accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.title: Render retained private branches in their reader's macro context
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.body: The guard is removed, but its reader's identity is left behind—an entertaining way to manufacture false memories. With merged readers Cara, Maukie and Pantalone, `{{#if char == "Maukie"}}{{char}} hid the compass{{/if}}` becomes `[Known only to Maukie: Cara hid the compass]`, because the later `resolveMacros` still uses `names[0]`. A variable guard enclosing a character-private branch is instead retained wholesale, so that branch still disappears for the wrong primary character or appears without its knowledge label. The added literal-only regression cannot detect either failure.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.fix_hint: Resolve reader-dependent conditions and substitutions before combining and labelling their resulting text; the primary character must not impersonate another reader's memory.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.label: tp-1689

accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.title: Apply union access to recap source eligibility as well
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.body: The admission rule now accepts any rememberer, while the source gate quietly continues demanding everyone. `prepareImpl` builds `eligibleIds` through `allowed(ctx, sources, audience)`, which excludes a message hidden from any member of the merged audience; its later scene filter still requires at least one such common source message. A scene fully visible to Maukie but wholly hidden from Pantalone therefore passes this new predicate and then vanishes, despite Maukie's valid access. Adding a character with hidden historical sources, or merging an individual chat with private history, still drops memories the documented union rule promises to recall.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.fix_hint: Judge recap source access using the present characters who remember that scene, while retaining the stricter visibility filter for live messages and raw excerpts.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.label: tp-3382

accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.title: Context trimming can amputate a private fragment's attribution
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.body: The new knowledge boundary exists only in a fragment's opening text, while constant-summary fitting still slices the compiled string into arbitrary head and tail excerpts. When a long shared prefix precedes a long `[Known only to Maukie: …]` fragment, `fitText` can keep shared text at the head and private text at the tail while discarding the opening label. The final prompt then carries private facts without the attribution promised for merged replies; the generous 12,000-token regression never forces this path.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.fix_hint: Fit annotated fragments as units, preserving their reader labels whenever any private content survives.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.label: real-1693

accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.title: Merged recall leaks a scene summary to a present reader its sources were hidden from
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.body:
Input: A merged group chat (ctx.individual false) with two or more present characters, where one character remembers a scene whose source messages are hidden from another present character via hiddenFromAICharacterIds, and the scene is not fully eligible for that other reader.
Failure: recallAudienceMatches now uses characters.some(...), so the scene passes the audience check for the other character. Its summary, which can state the hidden content, is then recalled into the other character's merged reply. The per-audience message filter does not stop this, because only the excerpt path is filtered.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.label: wrong-md1-leak

accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.title: Regression setup inserts duplicate character ids
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.body:
Input: Run the regression with the earlier setup already having inserted character rows with ids maukie, pantalone or narrator.
Failure: The new loop inserts those same ids into the characters table again. If the store enforces uniqueness, the test fails during setup and CI breaks.
accf6790ea062ccdeb60779228c7ff2565566cb8.label: wrong-ds2-dupkey

ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.title: Fit the new context floor to the Helper's input budget
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.body: The four-message floor can add roughly 4,000 tokens of prior-scene text even when the Helper has a valid 2,048-token input allowance. `visibilityTask()` trims only against the fixed 6,000-token limit, and `decideVisibility()` throws when the complete request fails `helper.fits()`: a small opening message that previously fit now receives no visibility decision and is permanently recorded with nobody hidden. A rather counterproductive admission policy for absent characters; the added regression uses short messages and a 16,384-token cap, so this failure escapes observation.
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.fix_hint: Fit optional preceding context against the resolved Helper request budget before asking, dropping or shortening older context while retaining the messages being decided.
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.label: real-1216-overflow

ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.title: Keep an exactly undecided score visible
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.body: The new confidence gate still admits a perfect tie. Both memory visibility call paths supply the connection's default threshold of 0.5, so an accepted probability of exactly 0.5 now hides the message, whereas the previous comparison left it visible. That contradicts the new uncertainty-keeps-visibility contract, and applyVisibility persists the result as already decided; the added 0.3 fixture never examines this boundary.
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.fix_hint: Refuse the tie before persisting a hide: use a strict boundary or an explicitly conservative absence cutoff, and exercise it in both Decision call paths.
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.label: plausible-1275

ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.title: Presence context now reaches into the previous scene
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.body:
Input: A new scene opens after a saved scene ends, so `scene` has no messages before `first`, while `before` is every earlier message in the whole chat.
Failure: `shown` now draws context from `before`, which is not limited to the current scene, so messages from the previous scene and from characters who have since left are sent as context. That can lead the presence model to misjudge who is present in the new scene. Earlier code kept context inside the scene, so this changes what the model sees.
ebb2187eddb461a59dc64c13a5ae3b50d4d61d11.label: wrong-ck1-prevscene

5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.title: Swipe number overrules the latest manual correction
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.body: An orderly procession of swipes is mistaken for an edit chronology. Edit location on swipe 1, switch to swipe 0 and correct it again, then regenerate: ascending swipe order applies swipe 1 last, so the older correction wins over the value just saved in the panel. The comment acknowledges this ceiling, but it directly contradicts the promised corrected-value baseline.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.fix_hint: Give manual edits an explicit precedence based on when they were made, rather than letting swipe numbering impersonate time.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.label: wrong-325-ponytail

5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.title: Retired edits can reactivate without another manual edit
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.body: The edit record survives a tracker rewrite even after its value stops matching, making retirement merely a temporary mismatch. Correct location to A, rerun trackers to B, then rerun them back to A: the preserved record matches again and regeneration unexpectedly overlays A, although the first rerun had retired that correction. _applyUpdate has the same dormant-record behavior, so the advertised one-way retirement is not enforced.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.fix_hint: Remove superseded edit entries when a successful nonmanual write changes their values; do not preserve them as dormant instructions.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.label: tp-518

5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.title: Retired edits revive when tracker output returns to their old value
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.body: A fascinatingly reversible retirement: this comparison suppresses an edit only while its row differs from the recorded value. Non-manual updates leave manualOverrides intact, and create now preserves that record on replacement, so a rerun changing an edited location from A to B retires it only until another rerun outputs A. Regeneration then reapplies A as a manual correction despite no intervening manual edit, contradicting the documented retirement rule.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.fix_hint: Retire changed edit entries when non-manual writes persist, including tracker paths that update snapshot columns directly; mere fingerprint inequality is not a tombstone.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.label: tp-518

5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.title: Clearing playerStats reconstructs an object instead of null
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.body: The API explicitly permits playerStats: null, but the per-key record cannot represent that whole-object clear. recordManualEdits fingerprints the removed keys, and this merge writes undefined for each one; JSON.stringify drops them and leaves playerStats as '{}' instead of null. Keys present only in the earlier regeneration baseline can even survive the clear, restoring data the panel removed.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.fix_hint: Represent a whole playerStats clear explicitly and preserve it when applying the overlay, while retaining distinct semantics for individual key deletion.
5263deed6ad5aba02ff74173c6dc1bcf91a04572.label: real-337

11a0693e1ae9bf40a15a98128677953a490b5f46.title: Private facts can escape through paraphrase
11a0693e1ae9bf40a15a98128677953a490b5f46.body: How reassuringly literal: the privacy gate only recognizes an exact sentence copied into a wider audience section, and even then ignores every sentence shorter than four words. A helper can rephrase a private fact—or copy a short secret verbatim—while leaving an innocuous sentence under the original condition; the section keys still match, so line 3400 accepts and persists the leak for readers who were never meant to know it.
11a0693e1ae9bf40a15a98128677953a490b5f46.fix_hint: Do not treat matching a few unchanged words as proof of unchanged access; reject unverified conditional rewrites or validate the facts in each reader scope before saving.
11a0693e1ae9bf40a15a98128677953a490b5f46.label: tp-3400

f481e3248b309689a4abae0f5603370ae0360dbc.title: Keep missing recaps restricted when Fix gets an unclear audience
f481e3248b309689a4abae0f5603370ae0360dbc.body: The access safeguard requires previousRecord.content, leaving missing and incomplete recaps outside the experiment's containment. In a group chat, summarize treats an omitted audience as every eligible character and sets audienceIssue; this branch saves that expanded audience when Fix creates the replacement. Adding the unresolved marker requests review but does not prevent recall, so an unclear answer can grant fresh access during the very operation that promises to preserve it.
f481e3248b309689a4abae0f5603370ae0360dbc.fix_hint: Apply the conservative audience rule to every unclear Fix result, using narrator-only access when no trustworthy prior audience exists.
f481e3248b309689a4abae0f5603370ae0360dbc.label: wrong-2251-7184
